entry.title: Help: Rainmeter Skins • Re: Help me fake 3D!
entry.content:
i'm trying to animate the meter, like shrink/expand the image vertices or sides to acomplish that
Well, strictly for the fake 3D perspective - animation on mouse over is a different thing, you'll need the Mouse plugin for getting coordinates in relation to a backrgound meter bigger than your card meter, and some well computed math involving projecting to approximate 3D perspective (i.e. to know how much to add or subtract from the original dimensions of the image, like below) - I think there's a solution for it: the MagickMeter plugin.

However, the process is a bit convoluted, since the plugin is badly outdated and won't work with newer versions of ImageMagick (which is the force powering that plugin). So, do the following (make sure to tick the "Add application directory to your system path" in the installation options of ImageMagick, as mentioned in the MagickMeter instructions from the above link):
- install the older ImageMagick 7.0.8-Q16 program from here
- install the skin here, for the latest 0.7.4.0 version of the MagickMeter plugin for Rainmeter
- after testing that skin and making sure it works as described there, use something like this:

Code: 

[Rainmeter]Update=1000AccurateText=1DynamicWindowSize=1[Perspective]Measure=PluginPlugin=MagickMeterImage=File #@#Card.png | Perspective (0+50),(0+25),(273-50),(0-25),(273-50),(408+25),(0+50),(408-25)UpdateDivider=-1DynamicVariables=1[Image]Meter=ImageMeasureName=PerspectiveUpdateDivider=-1
on a card image like (this is just cropped from the screenshot you posted earlier):
Card.png
that you copy as the C:\Users\[YourName]\Documents\Rainmeter\Skins\[YourSkin]\@Resources\Card.png file on your system.

It should result in something like this:
Card Perspective - Preview.jpg
Take into account that I intentionally set UpdateDivider=-1 in the MagickMeter measure. The measure will consume a LOT of your CPU if DynamicVariables=1 is set on it and any other update divider is used on the measure (it may even crash your Rainmeter because of that). Enabling dynamic variables on it will be needed for the animation based on the mouse coordinate values later on, so the measure should only be updated when needed.

As for the mouse coordinate based animation, that will be for either someone else or some other day. In the meantime, you can play with it and why not, try to achieve it yourself if impatient - just careful with the measure updates, don't abuse them.

Reference:
- https://github.com/khanhas/MagickMeter/wiki/Effects#perspective

entry.title: Help: Rainmeter Application • Re: 3d rotating app ring around planet wallpaper
entry.content:
Ahhh, now I know what it is, thanks for the video - I managed to replicate it myself. It's the fact that the ellipse is so ellongated / flattened and the icons so many (both things increasing the likehood of icons overlapping), that the counter-clockwise circular order regularly used for such scenarios:
curve-arrow perspective.jpg
comes into "conflict" with how things are perceived in a "real" 3D space (which this is not, as mentioned before), of things drawn from afar to upclose, essentially replicable by two semicircle orders going into opposite directions from upwards to downwards:
two-arrows perspective.jpg

Imagine the above would be in 3D perspective, and notice that in the 1st image (which is the order in which things are drawn now), based on the arrow's direction (which replicates the back to front layout of the current meters), on both the left and the right, icons that would be supposedly far away (i.e. in the upper half of the arc) would be drawn in front of icons that would be supposedly up close (i.e. in the lower half of the arc), since the former are closer to the arrow's end (which indicates the frontmost parts). On the other hand, the 2nd image is more similar to how things are perceived in real 3D space, where the arrow ends corresponding to the frontmost parts are in the lower half of the arc, which corresponds to the up close part of that shape, as typically represented in 3D schematics.

I'll think about ways to deal with this situation tomorrow - nice catch!
